title: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता — कर्मयोगः
titleEn: The Bhagavad Gītā — Chapter 3: The Yoga of Action
draftNote: Prepared by the Lectorium pipeline from the vulgate text, with a drafting pass, a reviewing pass and a mechanical gate; a printed-edition collation and audio are still to come. Use ⚑ correction on any verse to report a problem.
source: Text: the received (vulgate) text of the Bhagavadgītā, Mahābhārata 6.23–40, as read by Śaṅkara's commentary. Devanagari from Sanskrit Wikisource (भगवद्गीता/कर्मयोगः), collated verse by verse against the GRETIL romanized text based on the BORI critical edition (input Tokunaga, rev. J. Smith); every verse where the two differ carries a note giving the BORI reading, and every correction to the Wikisource text is named in its note. Collation against a pre-1930 printed edition is still to be done. Transliteration: IAST. The reading under each word gives the words with sandhi undone and compound members hyphenated, in the manner of the traditional pada-pāṭha. Pronunciation convention: classical Sanskrit as described in Whitney's Sanskrit Grammar (1889); no audio yet. Translations made fresh from the Sanskrit with Monier-Williams (1899), Apte (1890) and Śaṅkara's commentary for the traditional sense; no modern translation consulted.

sentences.t: अर्जुन उवाच
sentences.tr: arjuna uvāca
sentences.l: Arjuna said

morph.gloss: Arjuna, the third Pāṇḍava, the great archer (nom. sg.)

sentences.t:
ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन ।
तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥
sentences.tr:
jyāyasī cet karmaṇaḥ te matā buddhiḥ janārdana |
tat kim karmaṇi ghore mām niyojayasi keśava ||

morph.gloss: better, more excellent (comparative; nom. sg. fem., agreeing with buddhiḥ)
you (te: enclitic gen. sg. 'your, in your view'; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
to think (matā: past participle, nom. sg. fem. 'deemed, considered')
'rouser of men', an epithet of Kṛṣṇa (vocative)
terrible, dreadful (loc. sg., agreeing with karmaṇi)
to engage, urge, appoint (niyojayasi: causative present 2nd sg. 'you urge, you engage')
epithet of Kṛṣṇa, traditionally 'slayer of the demon Keśin' (vocative)

sentences.l: If more-excellent than-action, in-your-view, [is] wisdom, O Janārdana — then why into-terrible action me do-you-urge, O Keśava?
sentences.i: If wisdom is better than action in your eyes, Janārdana, why then do you urge me into this dreadful action, Keśava?
sentences.n: Arjuna reopens the question chapter 2 seemed to have closed. Cet karmaṇaḥ te matā buddhir, 'if wisdom is, in your view, better than action', refers back to 2.49-51's ranking of buddhi-yoga above ordinary action; Arjuna reads that teaching as an argument for withdrawal, which the rest of this chapter corrects. Janārdana ('rouser of men') and Keśava (traditionally 'slayer of the demon Keśin') are two more epithets of Kṛṣṇa, alongside the many already used in chapter 2.

sentences.t:
व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे ।
तदेकं वद निश्चित्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥
sentences.tr:
vyāmiśreṇa iva vākyena buddhim mohayasi iva me |
tat ekam vada niścitya yena śreyaḥ aham āpnuyām ||

morph.gloss: confused, mixed up (vyāmiśreṇa: instr. sg., 'with words that seem confused'; see note on the BORI reading)
to be confused (mohayasi: causative present 2nd sg. 'you seem to bewilder')
one, single (ekam: acc. sg. neut., 'that one thing')
to ascertain, decide (niścitya: gerund 'having decided for certain')
which (yena: instr. sg. neut. relative, 'by which')
the better thing, the good (nom. sg. neut.; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
to attain, reach (āpnuyām: optative 1st sg. 'I might attain')

sentences.l: With-speech that-seems-confused you-seem-to-bewilder my understanding; that one-thing tell, having-decided-for-certain, by-which the-better I-might-attain.
sentences.i: Your words seem to confuse me and bewilder my understanding. Tell me for certain the one thing by which I may attain what is truly best.
sentences.n: Vyāmiśreṇa iva vākyena, 'with speech that seems confused', and mohayasi iva, 'you seem to bewilder', repeat iva twice in one line — Arjuna feels, rather than flatly asserts, that Kṛṣṇa is contradicting himself. The vulgate reads vyāmiśreṇeva (vyāmiśreṇa + iva, 'as if confused'); the BORI critical edition reads vyāmiśreṇaiva instead (vyāmiśreṇa + eva, 'indeed confusing, indeed mixed'), a real difference in sense — eva asserts what iva only suggests.

sentences.t: श्रीभगवानुवाच
sentences.tr: śrībhagavān uvāca
sentences.l: The Blessed Lord said

morph.gloss: the Blessed One, the Lord — Kṛṣṇa's title as speaker (nom. sg. bhagavān; -n + u- written joined)

sentences.t:
लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ ।
ज्ञानयोगेन सांख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम् ॥
sentences.tr:
loke asmin dvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayā anagha |
jñāna-yogena sāṃkhyānām karma-yogena yoginām ||

morph.gloss: world (loke: loc. sg.; loke + a- → loke ' with avagraha)
to declare, teach (proktā: past participle, nom. sg. fem. 'declared', agreeing with niṣṭhā)
sinless, faultless (anagha: vocative, addressed to Arjuna; mayā + a- → mayā-)
yoga (jñāna-yoga: 'the yoga of knowledge', instr. sg.)
Sāṃkhya, the path of knowledge (gen. pl. 'for the followers of Sāṃkhya'; kept untranslated per convention)
yoga (karma-yoga: 'the yoga of action', instr. sg.)
one who practices yoga (gen. pl. 'for the yogins')

sentences.l: In-this world a-twofold path, formerly, [was] declared by-me, O sinless-one: by-the-yoga-of-knowledge, for-the-Sāṃkhyas; by-the-yoga-of-action, for-the-yogins.
sentences.i: In this world I have taught, from of old, a twofold path: for the followers of Sāṃkhya, the yoga of knowledge, and for those who practice yoga, the yoga of action.
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa answers Arjuna's confusion by naming, for the first time explicitly, the two paths already distinguished in substance at 2.39: jñāna-yoga, associated with the Sāṃkhyas, and karma-yoga, with the yogins. Sāṃkhya is named here as a proper term and kept untranslated per convention, alongside dharma, yoga, brahman and the guṇas; this chapter goes on to argue that karma-yoga, not withdrawal from action, is what a man in Arjuna's position needs (verses 4-8 give the reason why total inaction is not even possible).

sentences.t:
न कर्मणामनारम्भान्नैष्कर्म्यं पुरुषोऽश्नुते ।
न च संन्यसनादेव सिद्धिं समधिगच्छति ॥
sentences.tr:
na karmaṇām anārambhāt naiṣkarmyam puruṣaḥ aśnute |
na ca saṃnyasanāt eva siddhim samadhigacchati ||

morph.gloss: non-undertaking, non-commencement (anārambhāt: abl. sg. 'from not undertaking')
freedom from action, actionlessness (acc. sg. neut.; anārambhāt + n- → anārambhān n-)
a man, a person (nom. sg.; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
to attain, reach, enjoy (aśnute: present middle 3rd sg. 'attains')
to renounce (saṃnyasana: 'renunciation', saṃnyasanāt: abl. sg. 'from renunciation')

sentences.l: Not by-non-undertaking of-actions freedom-from-action does-a-man attain; nor by-renunciation-alone perfection does-he-reach.
sentences.i: A man does not attain freedom from action merely by abstaining from action, nor does he reach perfection by renunciation alone.
sentences.n: Naiṣkarmya, 'the state of action-lessness' (from niṣ-karma), names the goal Arjuna implicitly wants after chapter 2; the verse denies that simply not acting (anārambhāt), or formally renouncing (saṃnyasanāt), gets one there. This opens the section (through verse 8) arguing that action itself is unavoidable.

sentences.t:
न हि कश्चित्क्षणमपि जातु तिष्ठत्यकर्मकृत् ।
कार्यते ह्यवशः कर्म सर्वः प्रकृतिजैर्गुणैः ॥
sentences.tr:
na hi kaścit kṣaṇam api jātu tiṣṭhati akarma-kṛt |
kāryate hi avaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛti-jaiḥ guṇaiḥ ||

morph.gloss: a moment (kṣaṇam: adverbial acc. 'for a moment')
to stand, remain, exist (tiṣṭhati: present 3rd sg.; -i + a- → -y a-)
one who does not perform action, non-acting (nom. sg. bahuvrīhi)
to do, make (kāryate: causative passive present 3rd sg. 'is made to act')
powerless, not one's own master (avaśaḥ: nom. sg.)
born (prakṛti-ja: 'born of nature', instr. pl.; -aiḥ + g- → -air g-)
one of the three guṇas (instr. pl.; kept untranslated per convention)

sentences.l: For not anyone, even-for-a-moment, ever remains non-action-doing; everyone is-made-to-act, powerless, by-the-guṇas born-of-nature.
sentences.i: No one can remain, even for a moment, without acting; everyone is driven to act, powerless to stop, by the guṇas born of nature.
sentences.n: The reason behind verse 4's denial: action is not optional at all. Prakṛti-jair guṇaiḥ, 'by the guṇas born of nature (prakṛti)', is the poem's first mention of the three guṇas, kept untranslated per convention and developed at length in chapter 14; avaśaḥ, 'powerless, not his own master', underscores that even the wish to stop acting cannot succeed.

sentences.t:
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् ।
इन्द्रियार्थान्विमूढात्मा मिथ्याचारः स उच्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
karma-indriyāṇi saṃyamya yaḥ āste manasā smaran |
indriya-arthān vimūḍha-ātmā mithyā-cāraḥ saḥ ucyate ||

morph.gloss: sense-organ (karma-indriya: 'organ of action', acc. pl.; -a + i- → -e-)
who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative; -aḥ before ā- elided, plain y)
to sit, remain (āste: present middle 3rd sg.)
to remember, dwell on (smaran: present participle, nom. sg. masc. 'thinking of, dwelling on')
self, mind (vimūḍha-ātman: 'whose self is deluded', nom. sg.; -a + ā- → -ā-)
conduct, practice (mithyā-cāra: 'one of false conduct, a hypocrite', nom. sg.)
that, he (saḥ: nom. sg. masc.; the pronoun sa drops its visarga before any consonant)
to speak, call (ucyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is called')

sentences.l: The-organs-of-action having-restrained, who sits, with-the-mind dwelling-on the-objects-of-the-senses — whose-self-is-deluded, of-false-conduct, he is-called.
sentences.i: One who restrains the organs of action but sits dwelling in his mind on the objects of the senses — his mind confused, he is called a hypocrite.
sentences.n: This verse names the wrong response to verses 4-5: karma-indriyāṇi, 'the organs of action' (hands, feet, speech and so on, as distinct from the organs of perception, a distinction assumed but not spelled out here), can be restrained while the mind still dwells (smaran) on the sense-objects. Mithyācāraḥ, 'one of false conduct', is the poem's word for this kind of outward-only restraint — hypocrisy.

sentences.t:
यस्त्विन्द्रियाणि मनसा नियम्यारभतेऽर्जुन ।
कर्मेन्द्रियैः कर्मयोगमसक्तः स विशिष्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
yaḥ tu indriyāṇi manasā niyamya ārabhate arjuna |
karma-indriyaiḥ karma-yogam asaktaḥ saḥ viśiṣyate ||

morph.gloss: who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
to undertake, begin (ārabhate: present middle 3rd sg. 'undertakes'; niyamya + ā- → niyamyā-)
organ (karma-indriya: 'organ of action', instr. pl.; -a + i- → -e-)
yoga (karma-yoga: 'the yoga of action', acc. sg., object of ārabhate)
to excel, be distinguished (viśiṣyate: present passive 3rd sg.)

sentences.l: But-who, [his] senses with-the-mind having-restrained, undertakes the-yoga-of-action with-the-organs-of-action, O Arjuna, unattached — he excels.
sentences.i: But the man who controls his senses with his mind, Arjuna, and, unattached, engages the organs of action in the discipline of action — he is superior.
sentences.n: The positive counterpart to verse 6's hypocrite: the same restraint (niyamya, from the same root as saṃyamya in verse 6) is applied first to the mind, so that the organs of action can then be used, unattached (asaktaḥ), for karma-yoga itself — outward action joined to inward detachment, rather than outward inaction hiding inward craving.

sentences.t:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः ।
शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
sentences.tr:
niyatam kuru karma tvam karma jyāyaḥ hi akarmaṇaḥ |
śarīra-yātrā api ca te na prasiddhyet akarmaṇaḥ ||

morph.gloss: to prescribe, fix (niyata: past participle 'prescribed, fixed, obligatory', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with karma)
action (nom. sg., subject of the next clause)
better, more excellent (comparative; nom. sg. neut.; -aḥ before h- → -o)
journey, maintenance (śarīra-yātrā: 'the maintenance of the body', nom. sg.)
to succeed, be accomplished (prasiddhyet: optative 3rd sg. 'would be accomplished'; Wikisource's doubled dh; see note on the BORI reading prasidhyet, single dh)

sentences.l: The-prescribed action do, you; action [is] better, indeed, than-inaction; even the-maintenance-of-your-body would-not-be-accomplished without-action.
sentences.i: Perform the action that is your duty, for action is better than inaction; even the upkeep of your own body would be impossible without acting at all.
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa's first direct command to act: niyatam karma, 'the prescribed action', i.e. one's own duty (sva-dharma, named explicitly at verse 35). Śarīra-yātrā, 'the body's journey', a vivid compound for day-to-day bodily upkeep, makes the argument concrete: total inaction is not even physically possible. The Wikisource text reads na prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ, with a doubled dh (from the root sidh/sidhyati, 'to succeed'); the BORI critical edition reads na prasidhyed akarmaṇaḥ, with a single dh, the more regular form of the verb, with no difference of sense.

sentences.t:
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः ।
तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर ॥
sentences.tr:
yajña-arthāt karmaṇaḥ anyatra lokaḥ ayam karma-bandhanaḥ |
tad-artham karma kaunteya mukta-saṅgaḥ samācara ||

morph.gloss: purpose, sake (yajña-artha: 'the purpose of sacrifice', arthāt: abl. sg.; yajña + a- → yajñā-)
action (karmaṇaḥ: abl. sg.; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha, karmaṇo 'nyatra)
bond, fetter (karma-bandhana: 'bound by action', nom. sg.)
purpose, sake (tad-artham: 'for that purpose', adverbial acc.)
attachment, clinging (mukta-saṅga: 'free from attachment', nom. sg.)

sentences.l: Except-for-action-done-for-the-sake-of-sacrifice, this world [is] bound-by-action; for-that-purpose action, O son-of-Kuntī, free-from-attachment, perform!
sentences.i: This world is bound by action, except for action performed as sacrifice. Do your work for that purpose, Kaunteya, free from attachment.
sentences.n: Yajña, 'sacrifice', begins the chapter's extended treatment (through verse 16) of ritual sacrifice as the paradigm case of unattached action: an act done not for private gain but to sustain a larger order escapes karma-bandhana, 'the bondage of action'. Mukta-saṅgaḥ, 'free from attachment', restates verse 7's asaktaḥ in different words.

sentences.t:
सहयज्ञाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापतिः ।
अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधुक् ॥
sentences.tr:
saha-yajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purā uvāca prajāpatiḥ |
anena prasaviṣyadhvam eṣaḥ vaḥ astu iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk ||

morph.gloss: sacrifice (saha-yajña: 'together with sacrifice', acc. pl., bahuvrīhi describing prajāḥ)
'lord of creatures', the Vedic creator-deity (nom. sg.)
this (anena: instr. sg. 'by this', referring to yajña)
to bring forth, procreate (prasaviṣyadhvam: future middle 2nd pl. 'you shall multiply')
this (eṣaḥ: nom. sg., referring to yajña; prasaviṣyadhvam + e- written joined; like sa, eṣa/etad irregularly drops its visarga before the following consonant v-, rather than becoming -o)
you (vaḥ: enclitic dat. pl. 'to you'; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
to be (astu: imperative 3rd sg. 'let it be!'; astu + i- → astv i-)
to milk, yield (dhuk: 'that which yields', iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk: 'the yielder of desired things', nom. sg., like the wish-fulfilling cow)

sentences.l: Together-with-sacrifice creatures having-created, formerly said Prajāpati: 'By-this shall-you-multiply; this to-you let-it-be the-yielder-of-desired-wishes.'
sentences.i: In ancient times, Prajāpati, having brought forth creatures together with sacrifice, said: 'By this may you prosper; let this be the cow that grants your desires.'
sentences.n: Prajāpati, the Vedic creator-deity ('lord of creatures'), opens the chapter's account of the mutual sacrifice-cycle between gods and men (through verse 16) with a founding word to newborn creation: saha-yajñāḥ, 'together with sacrifice', casts humanity as created already bound to yajña as its means of flourishing. Iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk, 'the yielder of desired things', echoes the mythic kāmadhenu, the wish-fulfilling cow, casting sacrifice itself in that role.

sentences.t:
देवान्भावयतानेन ते देवा भावयन्तु वः ।
परस्परं भावयन्तः श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यथ ॥
sentences.tr:
devān bhāvayata anena te devāḥ bhāvayantu vaḥ |
parasparam bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ param avāpsyatha ||

morph.gloss: to cause to flourish, nourish (bhāvayata: causative imperative 2nd pl. 'nourish!')
this (anena: instr. sg. 'by this'; bhāvayata + a- → bhāvayatā-)
that, they (te: nom. pl., referring to devāḥ)
god (nom. pl.; visarga dropped before bh-)
to nourish, cause to flourish (bhāvayantu: causative imperative 3rd pl. 'let them nourish')
to nourish (bhāvayantaḥ: causative present participle, nom. pl. 'nourishing')
the good, the better thing (acc. sg. neut.)
to attain, obtain (avāpsyatha: future 2nd pl. 'you shall attain')

sentences.l: The-gods nourish by-this [sacrifice]; let-those gods nourish you [in return]; mutually nourishing, the-supreme good you-shall-attain.
sentences.i: Nourish the gods with this, and may the gods in turn nourish you; nourishing one another, you shall attain the highest good.
sentences.n: The reciprocal cycle stated directly: bhāvayata ... bhāvayantu, 'nourish ... let them nourish', the same causative verb used for both directions, presents sacrifice as mutual sustenance between gods and men, not a one-way payment. Parasparam bhāvayantaḥ, 'nourishing one another', generalizes the principle beyond ritual to any relation of mutual care.

sentences.t:
इष्टान्भोगान्हि वो देवा दास्यन्ते यज्ञभाविताः ।
तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥
sentences.tr:
iṣṭān bhogān hi vaḥ devāḥ dāsyante yajña-bhāvitāḥ |
taiḥ dattān apradāya ebhyaḥ yaḥ bhuṅkte stenaḥ eva saḥ ||

morph.gloss: you (vaḥ: enclitic dat. pl. 'to you'; -aḥ before d- → -o)
god (nom. pl.; visarga dropped before d-)
to give (dāsyante: future middle 3rd pl. 'will give')
propitiated, made to flourish (yajña-bhāvita: 'propitiated by sacrifice', nom. pl.)
that, they (taiḥ: instr. pl. 'by them', referring to the gods; -aiḥ + d- → -air d-)
to give (dattān: past participle, acc. pl. 'given [things]')
to not give in return (apradāya: negative gerund 'without giving back')
this, they (ebhyaḥ: dat. pl. 'to them'; apradāya + e- → apradāyai-)
who (nom. sg. masc. relative; -aḥ before bh- → -o)
a thief (nom. sg.; visarga elided before e-)

sentences.l: Desired enjoyments, indeed, to-you the-gods will-give, propitiated-by-sacrifice; by-them given, without-giving-in-return to-them, who enjoys [them] — a-thief indeed he [is].
sentences.i: The gods, gratified by sacrifice, will give you the enjoyments you desire. Whoever enjoys their gifts without giving anything back to them is nothing but a thief.
sentences.n: The cycle of verse 11 restated as an ethical claim: dattān apradāya, 'having received without giving [anything] in return', names the one who takes the gods' gifts (the natural bounty of rain and harvest, per verse 14) without offering sacrifice back — stenaḥ, 'a thief', a blunt word for what elsewhere might be softened as mere ingratitude.

sentences.t:
यज्ञशिष्टाशिनः सन्तो मुच्यन्ते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ।
भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥
sentences.tr:
yajña-śiṣṭa-aśinaḥ santaḥ mucyante sarva-kilbiṣaiḥ |
bhuñjate te tu agham pāpāḥ ye pacanti ātma-kāraṇāt ||

morph.gloss: remainder, what is left over (second compound member; śiṣṭa + a- → śiṣṭā-)
eater (yajña-śiṣṭa-aśin: 'eater of the remnants of sacrifice', nom. pl.)
to be (sant: present participle 'being', santaḥ: nom. pl.; -aḥ before m- → -o)
to release (mucyante: present passive 3rd pl. 'are freed')
sin, fault (sarva-kilbiṣa: 'all sins', instr. pl. 'from all sins')
to eat, enjoy (bhuñjate: present middle 3rd pl.)
sin, evil (agham: acc. sg., object of bhuñjate)
sinful, wicked (nom. pl.; visarga dropped before y-)
to cook (pacanti: present 3rd pl.; -i + ā- → -y ā-)
reason, cause (ātma-kāraṇāt: abl. sg. 'for their own sake')

sentences.l: Eaters-of-the-remnants-of-sacrifice, being, are-freed from-all-sins; but the-wicked eat sin, who cook for-their-own-sake.
sentences.i: Those who eat what remains after sacrifice are freed from all their faults; but those wicked people who cook only for themselves eat nothing but sin.
sentences.n: Yajña-śiṣṭa, 'what remains after sacrifice', names the practice of eating only after offering food first — the same discipline of unattached action, now given a concrete, domestic form. Pacanti ātma-kāraṇāt, 'cook for their own sake alone', is the plain opposite, and agham bhuñjate, 'eat sin', turns the very act of eating into a moral verdict.

sentences.t:
अन्नाद्भवन्ति भूतानि पर्जन्यादन्नसम्भवः ।
यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसमुद्भवः ॥
sentences.tr:
annāt bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyāt anna-sambhavaḥ |
yajñāt bhavati parjanyaḥ yajñaḥ karma-samudbhavaḥ ||

morph.gloss: food (annāt: abl. sg. 'from food'; -āt + bh- → -ād bh-)
to come to be, arise (bhavanti: present 3rd pl.)
the rain-god, rain (parjanyāt: abl. sg. 'from rain'; -āt + a- → -ād a-)
arising, origin (anna-sambhava: 'the arising of food', nom. sg.)
sacrifice (yajñāt: abl. sg. 'from sacrifice'; -āt + bh- → -ād bh-)
rain, the rain-god (nom. sg.; visarga before y- → -o)
arising, origination (karma-samudbhava: 'arisen from action', nom. sg.)

sentences.l: From-food come-to-be beings; from-rain [is] the-arising-of-food; from-sacrifice arises rain; sacrifice [is] arisen-from-action.
sentences.i: Beings arise from food; food is produced from rain; rain arises from sacrifice; and sacrifice arises from action.
sentences.n: A chain of dependence traced one step further back from verse 12's simple exchange: bhūtāni-anna-parjanya-yajña-karma, each said to bhavati, 'arise', from the one before — grounding the whole natural order in ritual action, and ritual action in turn in ordinary karma (deliberate human activity), traced one step further still in the next verse.

sentences.t:
कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् ।
तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
sentences.tr:
karma brahma-udbhavam viddhi brahma akṣara-samudbhavam |
tasmāt sarva-gatam brahma nityam yajñe pratiṣṭhitam ||

morph.gloss: brahman (first compound member; kept untranslated per convention)
arising, origin (brahma-udbhava: 'arisen from brahman', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with karma)
brahman (brahma: acc. sg. neut., a second object of viddhi; brahma + a- → brahmā-)
arising, origin (akṣara-samudbhava: 'arisen from the imperishable', acc. sg. neut.)
eternal, constant (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with brahma)
to be established, grounded (pratiṣṭhita: past participle, nom. sg. neut.)

sentences.l: Action, arisen-from-brahman, know; brahman, arisen-from-the-imperishable. Therefore the-all-pervading brahman, eternal, in-sacrifice [is] established.
sentences.i: Know that action arises from brahman, and that brahman arises from the imperishable. Therefore brahman, which pervades all things, is always grounded in sacrifice.
sentences.n: The chain from verse 14 now reaches brahman (kept untranslated per convention), traced back in turn to akṣara, 'the imperishable' — a still more fundamental reality, named here for the first time and taken up again at 8.3. The verse closes the causal chain begun at verse 9 by folding it back into sacrifice itself: sarva-gataṃ brahma ... yajñe pratiṣṭhitam, 'brahman, all-pervading, is grounded in sacrifice'. This is a hard verse to render literally: ब्रह्माक्षरसमुद्भवम् fuses two words, brahma (accusative, a second object of viddhi) and akṣara-samudbhavam. The word brahma shifts sense within the verse: Śaṅkara glosses the first occurrence (karma brahmodbhavam) specifically as the Veda — action arises from Vedic injunction — distinct from the cosmic, all-pervading brahman of the second line.

sentences.t:
एवं प्रवर्तितं चक्रं नानुवर्तयतीह यः ।
अघायुरिन्द्रियारामो मोघं पार्थ स जीवति ॥
sentences.tr:
evam pravartitam cakram na anuvartayati iha yaḥ |
aghāyuḥ indriya-ārāmaḥ mogham pārtha saḥ jīvati ||

morph.gloss: to set in motion (pravartita: causative past participle, acc. sg. neut. 'set in motion')
to keep turning, follow (anuvartayati: causative present 3rd sg.; -i + i- → -ī-)
life (agha-āyus: 'whose life is sin', aghāyuḥ: nom. sg.; -uḥ + i- → -ur i-)
delight, pleasure-garden (indriya-ārāma: 'delighting in the senses', nom. sg.; -a + ā- → -ā-; visarga before m- → -o)

sentences.l: Thus set-in-motion, the-wheel, who does-not-keep-turning here — sinful-of-life, delighting-in-the-senses, in-vain, O Pārtha, he lives.
sentences.i: Whoever, Pārtha, does not keep this wheel turning as it has been set in motion, living a life of sin and delighting only in his senses, lives in vain.
sentences.n: Cakra, 'the wheel' (of the sacrifice-cycle just described, verses 9-15), gives the chapter's teaching on sacrifice its closing image and warning: not to keep it turning (na anuvartayati) is named aghāyuḥ, 'living a life of sin' — the mirror image of the yajña-śiṣṭāśinaḥ of verse 13, who are freed from sin. Indriya-ārāmaḥ, 'delighting in the senses', names the private self-indulgence the sacrifice-cycle is meant to counter.

sentences.t:
यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः ।
आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
yaḥ tu ātma-ratiḥ eva syāt ātma-tṛptaḥ ca mānavaḥ |
ātmani eva ca santuṣṭaḥ tasya kāryam na vidyate ||

morph.gloss: who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
delight (ātma-rati: 'delighting in the self', ratiḥ: nom. sg.; -iḥ + e- → -ir e-)
to be (syāt: optative 3rd sg. 'might be'; -t + ā- → -d ā-)
satisfied, content (ātma-tṛpta: 'satisfied in the self', nom. sg.; -aḥ + c- → -aś c-)
a man, a human being (nom. sg.)
to be satisfied (santuṣṭa: past participle, nom. sg. 'content'; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
to do (kārya: gerundive 'that which must be done, a duty', nom. sg. neut.)
to exist, be found (vidyate: present passive 3rd sg.)

sentences.l: But-whoever, delighting-in-the-self alone, might-be, and satisfied-in-the-self, a-man — content in-the-self-alone — for-him a-duty not exists.
sentences.i: But the man who finds his delight in the self alone, who is satisfied in the self and content in the self alone — for him there is nothing left to do.
sentences.n: A limiting case introduced by yas tu, 'but whoever': the man who has actually reached ātma-rati, 'delight in the self' (a state, not merely a claim, as verse 18 stresses), genuinely has no kāryam, 'nothing that must be done'. This qualifies, rather than contradicts, verses 4-16, since such a man is exceedingly rare, and Arjuna — as the verses that follow make clear — is not yet him.

sentences.t:
नैव तस्य कृतेनार्थो नाकृतेनेह कश्चन ।
न चास्य सर्वभूतेषु कश्चिदर्थव्यपाश्रयः ॥
sentences.tr:
na eva tasya kṛtena arthaḥ na akṛtena iha kaścana |
na ca asya sarva-bhūteṣu kaścit artha-vyapāśrayaḥ ||

morph.gloss: to do (kṛta: past participle 'what is done', kṛtena: instr. sg. 'by what is done')
purpose, concern (arthaḥ: nom. sg.; kṛtena + a- → kṛtenā-; visarga before n- → -o)
not done, undone (akṛtena: instr. sg. 'by what is not done'; akṛtena + i- → akṛtene-)
reliance, recourse (artha-vyapāśraya: 'a reliance for [his own] interest', nom. sg.)

sentences.l: Not-at-all for-him, by-what's-done, [is-there] purpose; nor by-what's-not-done, here, any [purpose] whatsoever; and-not his, among-all-beings, any reliance-for-interest [exists].
sentences.i: For such a man, nothing depends on what he does, and nothing depends on what he leaves undone; he has no stake at all, among any being, in anything for his own sake.
sentences.n: This spells out what 'nothing to do' (kāryam, verse 17) actually means: not indifference to action itself, but the absence of artha, 'personal interest, purpose', in either doing (kṛtena) or not doing (akṛtena) — and no artha-vyapāśrayaḥ, 'reliance for [his own] interest', on any being. This is the standard the rest of the chapter, from verse 19, asks Arjuna to imitate even without yet having attained it.

sentences.t:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर ।
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
sentences.tr:
tasmāt asaktaḥ satatam kāryam karma samācara |
asaktaḥ hi ācaran karma param āpnoti pūruṣaḥ ||

morph.gloss: to do (kārya: gerundive 'that which is to be done', acc. sg. neut.)
action (acc. sg., in apposition to kāryam)
to perform, do (ācaran: present participle, nom. sg. 'performing')
a man, a person (nom. sg.; epic variant spelling)

sentences.l: Therefore, unattached, always, the-action-that-is-to-be-done, perform! Unattached, indeed, performing action, the-supreme attains, a-man.
sentences.i: Therefore, always perform the action that must be done, without attachment; for a man who acts without attachment attains the highest goal.
sentences.n: The chapter's practical conclusion so far, restating verse 9's asaktaḥ ... samācara almost verbatim, now generalized past sacrifice to kāryaṃ karma, 'action that is [one's] duty' at large. Param āpnoti, 'attains the supreme', names the reward directly — the same word used at verse 15 of brahman's ultimate source, now naming the goal for the man who acts unattached.

sentences.t:
कर्मणैव हि संसिद्धिमास्थिता जनकादयः ।
लोकसंग्रहमेवापि संपश्यन्कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
sentences.tr:
karmaṇā eva hi saṃsiddhim āsthitāḥ janaka-ādayaḥ |
loka-saṃgraham eva api sampaśyan kartum arhasi ||

morph.gloss: to be perfected (saṃsiddhi: 'perfection', saṃsiddhim: acc. sg.)
to resort to, attain, establish oneself in (āsthitāḥ: past participle, nom. pl. 'having attained')
Janaka, the philosopher-king of Videha (first compound member; janaka + ā- → janakā-)
beginning (ādayaḥ: 'those beginning with', i.e. 'and others', nom. pl.)
the holding-together, welfare (loka-saṃgraha: 'the world's welfare', acc. sg.)
to consider, have regard to (sampaśyan: present participle, nom. sg. 'considering')
to deserve, ought (arhasi: present 2nd sg. 'you ought')

sentences.l: By-action-alone, indeed, perfection attained, Janaka-and-others; the-welfare-of-the-world alone, indeed, even, considering, to-do you-ought.
sentences.i: It was by action alone that Janaka and others attained perfection. You too should act, with an eye only to the world's welfare.
sentences.n: Janaka, the legendary philosopher-king of Videha, famed in later tradition as one who ruled and acted while fully liberated, is offered as precedent: karmaṇā eva, 'by action alone' (not by abstaining), he reached saṃsiddhi, 'complete perfection'. Loka-saṃgraha, 'the holding-together of the world, the world's welfare', names for the first time the positive motive the chapter offers Arjuna in place of both personal gain and mere duty, developed through verse 26 and echoed again as Kṛṣṇa's own reason for acting in verses 22-24.

sentences.t:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः ।
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥
sentences.tr:
yat yat ācarati śreṣṭhaḥ tat tat eva itaraḥ janaḥ |
saḥ yat pramāṇam kurute lokaḥ tat anuvartate ||

morph.gloss: whatever (yat yat: doubled relative, distributive 'whatever'; -t + ā- → -d ā-)
the best, most excellent (śreṣṭhaḥ: nom. sg.; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
that (tat tat: acc. sg. neut. doubled, 'that very thing', correlative to yat yat; -t + e- → -d e-)
other, ordinary (itaraḥ: nom. sg.; eva + i- → eve-; visarga before j- → -o)
to make, set (kurute: present middle 3rd sg.)
world, people (lokaḥ: nom. sg.; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)

sentences.l: Whatever the-best-man does, that very-thing, indeed, the-ordinary person [does]; whatever standard he makes, the-world/people follow that.
sentences.i: Whatever a great man does, ordinary people do as well; whatever standard he sets, the world follows it.
sentences.n: A second precedent-argument follows Janaka's example directly: śreṣṭhaḥ, 'the best/most excellent [man]', sets pramāṇam, 'the standard, the measure', that itaraḥ janaḥ, 'the ordinary person', imitates — this is the general principle behind loka-saṃgraha (verse 20), and the reason a wise man's unattached action matters beyond himself.

sentences.t:
न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किंचन ।
नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि ॥
sentences.tr:
na me pārtha asti kartavyam triṣu lokeṣu kiṃcana |
na anavāptam avāptavyam varte eva ca karmaṇi ||

morph.gloss: 'son of Pṛthā', Arjuna (vocative; pārtha + a- → pārthā-)
to do (kartavya: gerundive 'that which must be done, a duty', nom. sg. neut.)
to not have attained (anavāpta: past participle 'unobtained', nom. sg. neut.)
to attain (avāptavya: gerundive 'that must be attained', nom. sg. neut.)
to be occupied, engaged (varte: present middle 1st sg. 'I remain engaged'; its final -e reduces to -a before the following eva)

sentences.l: Not for-me, O Pārtha, there-is a-duty-to-be-done, in-the-three worlds, anything [whatsoever] — nothing-unobtained-to-be-obtained — [yet] I-remain-engaged, indeed, and, in-action.
sentences.i: There is nothing at all in the three worlds, Pārtha, that I must do, nothing unattained that I need attain — and yet I go on acting.
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa now gives his own case as the ultimate instance of verses 20-21's principle: precisely because he has nothing left to gain (nānavāptam avāptavyam, 'nothing unattained to be attained'), his continued action can only be for loka-saṃgraha, the world's sake, developed through verse 24. Varta here is varte, 'I remain engaged' (vṛt), its final -e reduced to -a before the following eva.

sentences.t:
यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः ।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥
sentences.tr:
yadi hi aham na varteyam jātu karmaṇi atandritaḥ |
mama vartma anuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ ||

morph.gloss: to be occupied, engaged (varteyam: optative 1st sg. 'I might remain engaged')
path, track (vartma: nom. sg. neut.; vartma + a- → vartmā-)
a man, a human being (nom. pl.)

sentences.l: If, indeed, I not might-be-engaged, ever, in-action, untiring — my path they-follow, men, O Pārtha, in-every-way.
sentences.i: For if I were not to keep acting, untiringly, at all times, Pārtha, people would follow my path in every way.
sentences.n: A conditional continuing from verse 22: Kṛṣṇa's own ceasing to act — as the ultimate śreṣṭhaḥ of verse 21 — would not be neutral but actively destructive, since manuṣyāḥ ... anuvartante, 'men follow', whatever standard he sets; the consequence is spelled out concretely in the next verse.

sentences.t:
उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् ।
संकरस्य च कर्ता स्यामुपहन्यामिमाः प्रजाः ॥
sentences.tr:
utsīdeyuḥ ime lokāḥ na kuryām karma cet aham |
saṃkarasya ca kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ ||

morph.gloss: to perish, sink, collapse (utsīdeyuḥ: optative 3rd pl. 'would perish'; -uḥ + i- → -ur i-)
world, people (nom. pl.; visarga dropped before n-)
to do (kuryām: optative 1st sg. 'I might do')
to do (kartṛ: agent noun 'doer', kartā: nom. sg.)
to be (syām: optative 1st sg. 'I might be')
to destroy, harm (upahanyām: optative 1st sg. 'I might destroy')

sentences.l: Would-perish these worlds, if not I-might-do action, if I; of-confusion and a-doer I-might-be; I-might-destroy these creatures.
sentences.i: If I did not act, these worlds would collapse; I would be the cause of chaos, and I would destroy all these creatures.
sentences.n: The concrete consequence of verse 23's hypothesis: saṃkara, 'confusion, intermingling' (a term used elsewhere of the mixing of social classes, treated by later tradition as a great social evil, e.g. 1.41-43), and the destruction of prajāḥ, 'creatures, subjects' — the stakes of a great man's example (verse 21) taken to their limit.

sentences.t:
सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत ।
कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम् ॥
sentences.tr:
saktāḥ karmaṇi avidvāṃsaḥ yathā kurvanti bhārata |
kuryāt vidvān tathā asaktaḥ cikīrṣuḥ loka-saṃgraham ||

morph.gloss: not knowing, unwise, ignorant (avidvāṃsaḥ: nom. pl.; visarga before y- → -o)

words.reading: kuryāt vidvān tathā asaktaḥ cikīrṣuḥ loka-saṃgraham

glyphs.tr: kuryāt vidvān tathā asaktaḥ cikīrṣuḥ loka-saṃgraham

morph.gloss: to do, act (kuryāt: optative 3rd sg. 'should act'; -t + v- → -d v-)
knowing, wise (vidvān: nom. sg. 'the wise man'; -n + t- → -ṃs t-)
to do (cikīrṣu: desiderative adjective 'wishing to act, desiring to promote', cikīrṣuḥ: nom. sg.; -uḥ + l- → -ur l-)
holding-together, welfare (loka-saṃgraha: 'the world's welfare', acc. sg., object of cikīrṣuḥ)

sentences.l: Attached, in-action, the-unwise, just-as act, O Bhārata; should-act, the-wise-man, likewise, unattached, desiring-to-promote the-welfare-of-the-world.
sentences.i: Just as the ignorant act with attachment to their work, Bhārata, so the wise man should act without attachment, wishing to uphold the welfare of the world.
sentences.n: Loka-saṃgraha, 'the world's welfare' (already named at verse 20), returns as the wise man's explicit motive — the positive answer to the question implicit since verse 17: if the truly wise have nothing left to gain, why should they act at all? Cikīrṣuḥ, 'desiring to do, wishing to promote' (a desiderative formation from kṛ), marks this as deliberate, chosen action, not passive drift.

sentences.t:
न बुद्धिभेदं जनयेदज्ञानां कर्मसङ्गिनाम् ।
जोषयेत्सर्वकर्माणि विद्वान्युक्तः समाचरन् ॥
sentences.tr:
na buddhi-bhedam janayet ajñānām karma-saṅginām |
joṣayet sarva-karmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācaran ||

morph.gloss: splitting, division, disturbance (buddhi-bheda: 'a disturbance of understanding', acc. sg.)
to cause to arise, produce (janayet: causative optative 3rd sg.; -t + a- → -d a-)
not knowing, ignorant (ajñānām: gen. pl. 'of the ignorant')
attached, clinging (karma-saṅgin: 'attached to action', gen. pl.)
to delight in, engage in (joṣayet: causative optative 3rd sg. 'should cause to delight in, should encourage')
knowing, wise (vidvān: nom. sg. 'the wise man')
to join, discipline (yukta: past participle 'disciplined, joined [in yoga]', yuktaḥ: nom. sg.)
to perform (samācaran: present participle, nom. sg. 'performing')

sentences.l: Not a-disturbance-of-understanding should-he-cause, of-the-ignorant, attached-to-action; should-encourage-in all-actions, the-wise-man, disciplined, performing [them himself].
sentences.i: Let the wise man not disturb the minds of the ignorant who are attached to their work; disciplined himself, and acting, let him encourage them in all their actions.
sentences.n: This states the wise man's social responsibility directly: buddhi-bhedam, 'a splitting of understanding', would only confuse ajñānāṃ karma-saṅginām, 'the ignorant who are attached to action', if suddenly told the truth of verses 17-18 (that action ultimately does not matter to the wise). Joṣayet, 'should encourage [them] to delight in', urges the wise man instead to keep performing action visibly himself (samācaran) as an example, per verses 20-21, rather than preach detachment to those not ready for it.

sentences.t:
प्रकृतेः क्रियमाणानि गुणैः कर्माणि सर्वशः ।
अहंकारविमूढात्मा कर्ताहमिति मन्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāni guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ |
ahaṃkāra-vimūḍha-ātmā kartā aham iti manyate ||

morph.gloss: to do (kriyamāṇa: present passive participle 'being done', nom. pl. neut.)
one of the three guṇas (instr. pl.; kept untranslated per convention)
ego, the sense of 'I' (first compound member)
self, mind (ahaṃkāra-vimūḍha-ātman: 'whose self is deluded by egoism', nom. sg.; -a + ā- → -ā-)
to do (kartṛ: agent noun 'doer', kartā: nom. sg.; kartā + a- → kartā-)

sentences.l: By-nature, being-done, by-the-guṇas, actions, in-every-way; whose-self-is-deluded-by-egoism, '[the] doer I [am]' — thus thinks.
sentences.i: Actions are, in every way, performed by the guṇas of nature; but a man whose mind is confused by egoism thinks, 'I am the doer.'
sentences.n: The chapter's first extended treatment of the guṇas (kept untranslated per convention; named individually only from chapter 14 on) as the true agents of all action, in contrast to ahaṃkāra, 'egoism' ('the I-maker'), which falsely claims agency for the self. Kartāham iti manyate, '[he] thinks, "I am the doer"', names precisely the error the next two verses correct.

sentences.t:
तत्त्ववित्तु महाबाहो गुणकर्मविभागयोः ।
गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ॥
sentences.tr:
tattva-vit tu mahā-bāho guṇa-karma-vibhāgayoḥ |
guṇāḥ guṇeṣu vartante iti matvā na sajjate ||

morph.gloss: to know (vit: 'knowing', tattva-vit: 'knower of the truth', nom. sg.)
one of the three guṇas (first compound member; kept untranslated)
distinction, division (guṇa-karma-vibhāga: 'the distinction between the guṇas and their actions', gen. dual)
one of the three guṇas (nom. pl.; kept untranslated; visarga dropped before g-)
one of the three guṇas (loc. pl.; kept untranslated per convention)
to act, operate (vartante: present middle 3rd pl.; -e + i- → -a i-)
to cling, become attached (sajjate: present middle 3rd sg.)

sentences.l: But-the-knower-of-the-truth, O mighty-armed-one, regarding-the-distinction-between-the-guṇas-and-their-actions, 'the-guṇas upon-the-guṇas act' — thus having-considered, not he-clings.
sentences.i: But the man who knows the truth about the guṇas and their actions, mighty-armed one, thinking 'the guṇas merely act upon the guṇas,' does not become attached.
sentences.n: The corrective to verse 27's error: tattva-vit, 'the knower of the truth' (about guṇa-karma-vibhāga, 'the distinction between the guṇas and their actions', i.e. that guṇas act on guṇas, not the self on anything), reaches na sajjate, 'does not cling', exactly by seeing the mechanism verse 27 described — knowledge itself, not extra effort, is what removes attachment.

sentences.t:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसंमूढाः सज्जन्ते गुणकर्मसु ।
तानकृत्स्नविदो मन्दान्कृत्स्नविन्न विचालयेत् ॥
sentences.tr:
prakṛteḥ guṇa-saṃmūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇa-karmasu |
tān akṛtsna-vidaḥ mandān kṛtsna-vit na vicālayet ||

morph.gloss: one of the three guṇas (first compound member; kept untranslated)
deluded, confused (guṇa-saṃmūḍha: 'deluded by the guṇas', nom. pl.)
to cling, become attached (sajjante: present middle 3rd pl.)
one of the three guṇas (first compound member; kept untranslated)
action (guṇa-karman: 'the actions of the guṇas', loc. pl.)
knowing (akṛtsna-vid: 'of incomplete knowledge', vidaḥ: acc. pl.; visarga before m- → -o)
knowing (kṛtsna-vit: 'one of complete knowledge', nom. sg.; -t + n- → -n n-)
to shake, waver (vicālayet: causative optative 3rd sg. 'should cause to waver, should unsettle')

sentences.l: Deluded-by-the-guṇas of-nature, they-cling to-the-actions-of-the-guṇas; those of-incomplete-knowledge, the-dull, one-of-complete-knowledge should-not-unsettle.
sentences.i: Those deluded by the guṇas of nature cling to what the guṇas do; but let the man of complete knowledge not unsettle those of partial understanding, the slow-witted.
sentences.n: This closes the section begun at verse 26 with the same instruction restated in the guṇa-vocabulary just introduced: akṛtsna-vidaḥ, 'those of incomplete knowledge' — the same ajñānām, 'the ignorant', of verse 26 — should not be vicālayet, 'made to waver', by a kṛtsna-vit, 'one of complete knowledge', showing off what they are not ready to hear.

sentences.t:
मयि सर्वाणि कर्माणि संन्यस्याध्यात्मचेतसा ।
निराशीर्निर्ममो भूत्वा युध्यस्व विगतज्वरः ॥
sentences.tr:
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasya adhyātma-cetasā |
nirāśīḥ nirmamaḥ bhūtvā yudhyasva vigata-jvaraḥ ||

morph.gloss: to lay down, surrender (saṃnyasya: gerund 'having laid down'; saṃnyasya + a- → saṃnyasyā-)
pertaining to the self, concerning the supreme self (first compound member)
mind (adhyātma-cetas: 'with a mind fixed on the self', instr. sg.)
free from desire, without expectation (nirāśīḥ: nom. sg.; -īḥ + n- → -īr n-)
free from the sense of 'mine' (nirmamaḥ: nom. sg.; visarga before bh- → -o)
to depart, go away (vigata: past participle 'gone, departed', first compound member)
fever, anguish (vigata-jvara: 'free from the fever [of anguish]', nom. sg.)

sentences.l: In-me all actions having-laid-down, with-a-mind-fixed-on-the-self, free-from-desire, free-from-mine-ness, having-become, fight! — free-from-anguish.
sentences.i: Surrendering all your actions to me, with your mind fixed on the self, free from desire and free from any sense of 'mine,' fight — and be free of anguish.
sentences.n: The section on action opened at verse 4 closes with a command directed at Arjuna himself, echoing the house rendering of 2.47 on acting without craving for the fruit: mayi ... saṃnyasya, 'having surrendered all actions in me', anticipates the fuller teaching on surrender to Kṛṣṇa personally that develops from chapter 7 on. Vigata-jvaraḥ, 'free from the fever [of anguish]', gives that anguish a vivid, almost physical name.

sentences.t:
ये मे मतमिदं नित्यमनुतिष्ठन्ति मानवाः ।
श्रद्धावन्तोऽनसूयन्तो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि कर्मभिः ॥
sentences.tr:
ye me matam idam nityam anutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ |
śraddhāvantaḥ anasūyantaḥ mucyante te api karmabhiḥ ||

morph.gloss: to think (mata: 'opinion, doctrine', matam: acc. sg. neut.)
to practice, follow, carry out (anutiṣṭhanti: present 3rd pl.)
a man, a human being (nom. pl.)
possessed of faith, faithful (śraddhāvantaḥ: nom. pl.; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
not carping, free from envy or fault-finding (anasūyantaḥ: present participle nom. pl.; visarga before m- → -o)
to release (mucyante: present passive 3rd pl. 'are freed')
that, they (te: nom. pl.; -e + a- → -e with avagraha)

sentences.l: Who my this doctrine constantly follow, men, faithful, uncomplaining — they too are-freed from-actions.
sentences.i: Those who constantly follow this teaching of mine, with faith and without envy — they too are freed from the bondage of action.
sentences.n: The teaching just given (verses 4-30) is now offered its own reward, addressed to any follower, not only Arjuna: śraddhāvantaḥ, 'possessed of faith', and anasūyantaḥ, 'free from envy, fault-finding', are the two qualities required; mucyante ... karmabhiḥ, 'are freed from actions', recalls karma-bandhanaḥ, 'bound by action', from verse 9.

sentences.t:
ये त्वेतदभ्यसूयन्तो नानुतिष्ठन्ति मे मतम् ।
सर्वज्ञानविमूढांस्तान्विद्धि नष्टानचेतसः ॥
sentences.tr:
ye tu etat abhyasūyantaḥ na anutiṣṭhanti me matam |
sarva-jñāna-vimūḍhān tān viddhi naṣṭān acetasaḥ ||

morph.gloss: this (etat: acc. sg. neut.; -t + a- → -d a-)
to carp at, find fault with (abhyasūyantaḥ: present participle, nom. pl.; visarga before n- → -o)
to think (mata: 'opinion, doctrine', matam: acc. sg. neut.)
deluded, confused (sarva-jñāna-vimūḍha: 'deluded in all knowledge', acc. pl.; -n + t- → -ṃs t-)
to be lost, perish (naṣṭa: past participle 'lost, ruined', naṣṭān: acc. pl.)

sentences.l: But-who, this finding-fault-with, do-not follow my doctrine — deluded-in-all-knowledge, those, know! lost, senseless.
sentences.i: But those who find fault with this teaching and do not follow it — know them to be blind to all wisdom, lost, and without understanding.
sentences.n: The negative counterpart to verse 31: abhyasūyantaḥ, 'finding fault, carping' (the opposite of verse 31's anasūyantaḥ), leads not merely to missing a benefit but to naṣṭān acetasaḥ, 'lost, senseless' — the chapter's harshest judgment on the willfully resistant listener.

sentences.t:
सदृशं चेष्टते स्वस्याः प्रकृतेर्ज्ञानवानपि ।
प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥
sentences.tr:
sadṛśam ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛteḥ jñānavān api |
prakṛtim yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kim kariṣyati ||

morph.gloss: in accordance with, similar to (adverbial acc.)
to act, strive, behave (ceṣṭate: present middle 3rd sg.)
one's own (svasyāḥ: gen. sg. fem., agreeing with prakṛteḥ)
possessed of knowledge, learned (jñānavān: nom. sg.)
to restrain, suppress (nigraha: 'restraint, suppression', nom. sg.)
to do, accomplish (kariṣyati: future 3rd sg. 'will accomplish')

sentences.l: In-accordance-with acts, his-own nature, even-the-learned-man; nature follow, beings; restraint what will-accomplish?
sentences.i: Even a man of knowledge acts according to his own nature; all beings follow their nature — what good is forcible restraint?
sentences.n: A candid limit on the teaching just given (verses 27-29): jñānavān api, 'even the learned/wise man', still acts sadṛśaṃ svasyāḥ prakṛteḥ, 'in accordance with his own nature' — knowledge changes how one relates to action (verse 28), not the underlying nature (prakṛti) itself. Nigrahaḥ, 'forcible restraint, suppression', is shown here to be largely futile against it, setting up verse 34's more targeted advice.

sentences.t:
इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियस्यार्थे रागद्वेषौ व्यवस्थितौ ।
तयोर्न वशमागच्छेत्तौ ह्यस्य परिपन्थिनौ ॥
sentences.tr:
indriyasya indriyasya arthe rāga-dveṣau vyavasthitau |
tayoḥ na vaśam āgacchet tau hi asya paripanthinau ||

morph.gloss: a sense (indriyasya: gen. sg., repeated distributively 'of each and every sense'; -a + i- → -e-)
object (arthe: loc. sg. 'in its object'; -a + a- → -ā-)
aversion, hatred (rāga-dveṣa: 'passion and aversion', nom. dual)
to be fixed, established (vyavasthita: past participle, nom. dual)
that, they (tayoḥ: gen. dual, referring to rāga and dveṣa; -oḥ + n- → -or n-)
control, power (vaśam: acc. sg., object of āgacchet)
to come under, fall under (āgacchet: optative 3rd sg. 'should come under'; āgacchet + t- → āgacchett-)
one who lies in wait on the road, an ambusher (nom. dual, 'the two waylayers')

sentences.l: For-each-sense, in-its-object, passion-and-aversion [stand] fixed; let-one-not come-under-the-control of-these-two, for-these-two, indeed, [are] his two-waylayers.
sentences.i: Passion and aversion are fixed toward the objects of each sense; one should not come under the sway of these two, for they lie in ambush as one's true enemies.
sentences.n: The targeted advice that follows from verse 33's admission that total suppression is futile: rāga and dveṣa, 'passion (attraction) and aversion' (ordinary vocabulary, not among the untranslated terms), are what actually need controlling, sense by sense, rather than the senses' contact with objects as such. Paripanthinau, 'the two who lie in wait on the road', a vivid image of ambush, names them as enemies more dangerous than any external one, anticipating verse 37's identification of the real enemy.

sentences.t:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
sentences.tr:
śreyān sva-dharmaḥ viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt su-anuṣṭhitāt |
svadharme nidhanam śreyaḥ paradharmaḥ bhaya-āvahaḥ ||

morph.gloss: dharma, duty (sva-dharma: 'one's own dharma', nom. sg.; visarga before v- → -o)
deficient, lacking merit, imperfectly performed (nom. sg.)
dharma, duty (para-dharma: 'another's dharma', abl. sg. 'than another's dharma')
to perform, practice (anuṣṭhita: past participle 'performed', su-anuṣṭhita: 'well-performed', abl. sg.; su + a- → sva-)
dharma, duty (sva-dharma: loc. sg. 'in one's own dharma')
dharma, duty (para-dharma: 'another's dharma', nom. sg.; visarga before bh- → -o)

sentences.l: Better, one's-own-dharma, deficient, than-another's-dharma well-performed; in-one's-own-dharma, death, [is] better — another's-dharma [is] danger-bringing.
sentences.i: It is better to do one's own dharma imperfectly than another's well; death while doing one's own dharma is better — another's dharma is fraught with danger.
sentences.n: The chapter's summary maxim on sva-dharma (already named in substance at verse 8, and taken up again at 18.47 near the poem's close). Dharma here is explicitly relative to the person: para-dharma, 'another's dharma' (a duty not one's own by class and station), is bhaya-āvahaḥ, 'danger-bringing', however well performed, because it is not truly one's own. Sva-dharma is left untranslated per convention, in the personal-duty sense of dharma rather than the cosmic-order sense used elsewhere.

sentences.t: अर्जुन उवाच
sentences.tr: arjuna uvāca
sentences.l: Arjuna said

morph.gloss: Arjuna, the third Pāṇḍava, the great archer (nom. sg.)

sentences.t:
अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः ।
अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥
sentences.tr:
atha kena prayuktaḥ ayam pāpam carati pūruṣaḥ |
anicchan api vārṣṇeya balāt iva niyojitaḥ ||

morph.gloss: to impel, drive (prayukta: past participle 'impelled, urged', nom. sg.; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
a man, a person (nom. sg.; epic variant spelling)
not wishing, unwilling (anicchan: present participle, nom. sg.; -n + a- written -nn-)
force, strength (balāt: abl. sg. 'by force'; -āt + i- → -ād i-)
to impel, compel (niyojita: causative past participle 'compelled, impelled', nom. sg.)

sentences.l: Now, by-what, impelled, this — sin does-commit, a-man, unwilling, even, O descendant-of-Vṛṣṇi — by-force, as-it-were, compelled?
sentences.i: Then what is it, Vārṣṇeya, that impels a man to commit sin, even against his will, as if driven to it by force?
sentences.n: A new question opens the chapter's final movement: Arjuna picks up the language of verses 27 and 33-34 (being driven by something other than one's own choice) and asks directly what that something is. Vārṣṇeya, 'descendant of Vṛṣṇi' (Kṛṣṇa's clan), is a new epithet of Kṛṣṇa in this chapter; balād iva niyojitaḥ, 'as if compelled by force', anticipates Kṛṣṇa's answer at verse 37 — not literal external compulsion, but something that feels like it.

sentences.t: श्रीभगवानुवाच
sentences.tr: śrībhagavān uvāca
sentences.l: The Blessed Lord said

morph.gloss: the Blessed One, the Lord — Kṛṣṇa's title as speaker (nom. sg. bhagavān; -n + u- written joined)

sentences.t:
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः ।
महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥
sentences.tr:
kāmaḥ eṣaḥ krodhaḥ eṣaḥ rajaḥ-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ |
mahā-aśanaḥ mahā-pāpmā viddhi enam iha vairiṇam ||

morph.gloss: desire (nom. sg.; visarga elided before e-)
this (eṣaḥ: nom. sg. masc.; like the pronoun sa, eṣa/etad irregularly drops its visarga before any consonant, here k-)
anger (nom. sg.; visarga elided before e-)
this (eṣaḥ: nom. sg. masc.; like the pronoun sa, eṣa/etad irregularly drops its visarga before any consonant, here r-)
rajas, the guṇa of passion and activity (rajaḥ: first compound member; kept untranslated as guṇa-vocabulary; -aḥ + g- → -o g-)
arising, born of (rajo-guṇa-samudbhava: 'born of the guṇa rajas', nom. sg.)
great (first compound member; mahā + a- → mahā-)
eater, devourer (mahā-aśana: 'great devourer, insatiable', nom. sg.; visarga before m- → -o)
to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg. 'know!'; -i + e- → -y e-)

sentences.l: Desire, this; anger, this — arisen-from-the-guṇa-rajas; great-devourer, greatly-sinful — know it, here, [as] the-enemy.
sentences.i: It is desire, it is anger, born of the guṇa rajas — insatiable and deeply sinful; know this to be the enemy here.
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa's answer identifies the force behind verse 36's 'as if compelled by force' precisely: kāma, 'desire', which shows itself as krodha, 'anger', is traced to rajo-guṇa, 'the guṇa rajas' (the second of the three guṇas, named individually here for the first time, though still untranslated per convention and only formally defined in chapter 14). Vairiṇam, 'the enemy', gives concrete shape to the paripanthinau, 'the two waylayers', of verse 34. This is among the poem's most quoted lines, the companion, several chapters on, to 16.21's 'triple gate to hell' (kāma, krodha, lobha); its doubled kāma eṣaḥ krodha eṣaḥ shows the same irregularity already met in sa/saḥ (e.g. verse 6 above, and chapters 1-2): eṣaḥ, like sa, drops its visarga before any following consonant rather than converting it in the usual way.

sentences.t:
धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथादर्शो मलेन च ।
यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥
sentences.tr:
dhūmena āvriyate vahniḥ yathā ādarśaḥ malena ca |
yathā ulbena āvṛtaḥ garbhaḥ tathā tena idam āvṛtam ||

morph.gloss: smoke (dhūmena: instr. sg. 'by smoke'; dhūmena + ā- → dhūmenā-)
to cover, envelop (āvriyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is covered')
mirror (ādarśaḥ: nom. sg.; visarga before m- → -o)
the caul, amnion (ulbena: instr. sg. 'by the caul'; ulbena + ā- → ulbenā-)
to cover (āvṛta: past participle 'covered', nom. sg.; visarga before g- → -o)
embryo, fetus, womb (nom. sg.; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
that (tena: instr. sg. 'by that'; tena + i- → tene-)
to cover (āvṛta: past participle, nom. sg. neut. 'covered'; idam + ā- → idamā-)

sentences.l: By-smoke is-covered fire, just-as a-mirror by-dust; just-as by-the-caul covered [is] the-embryo, so by-that this [is] covered.
sentences.i: As fire is veiled by smoke and a mirror by dust, and as an embryo is covered by its caul, so is this covered by that.
sentences.n: Three similes in ascending order of how deeply the covering hides what it covers — smoke over fire (removable at a touch), dust over a mirror (needing a wipe), the caul over an embryo (an organic, inseparable covering). The verse deliberately leaves 'this' (idam) and 'that' (tena) unnamed; only verse 39 identifies them as jñānam, 'knowledge', and kāma, 'desire' — a suspense the translation preserves rather than resolving early.

sentences.t:
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा ।
कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥
sentences.tr:
āvṛtam jñānam etena jñāninaḥ nitya-vairiṇā |
kāma-rūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇa analena ca ||

morph.gloss: to cover (āvṛta: past participle, nom. sg. neut. 'covered')
one who knows, a wise man (gen. sg.; visarga before n- → -o)
form, shape (kāma-rūpa: 'having the form of desire', instr. sg.)
hard to fill, insatiable (duṣpūreṇa: instr. sg.; duṣpūreṇa + a- → duṣpūreṇā-)

sentences.l: Covered, [is] knowledge, by-this, of-the-knower, by-[his]-constant-enemy — in-the-form-of-desire, O son-of-Kuntī, insatiable, like-a-fire.
sentences.i: The wise man's knowledge is veiled by this, its constant enemy in the shape of desire — a fire, Kaunteya, that is never filled.
sentences.n: The chapter's central identification, resolving verse 38's riddle: kāma-rūpeṇa, 'in the form of desire', names what covers jñāna, while duṣpūreṇa analena, 'an insatiable fire', gives desire two more images at once — never satisfied (pūra, 'filling') and consuming (anala, 'fire'), the same fire-image already used literally in verse 38's first simile.

sentences.t:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरस्याधिष्ठानमुच्यते ।
एतैर्विमोहयत्येष ज्ञानमावृत्य देहिनम् ॥
sentences.tr:
indriyāṇi manaḥ buddhiḥ asya adhiṣṭhānam ucyate |
etaiḥ vimohayati eṣaḥ jñānam āvṛtya dehinam ||

morph.gloss: mind (nom. sg. neut.; visarga before b- → -o)
this, it (asya: gen. sg., referring to kāma, 'its'; asya + a- → asyā-)
to stand upon (adhiṣṭhāna: 'seat, abode, basis', nom. sg. neut.)
to speak, call (ucyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is called')
this (etaiḥ: instr. pl. 'by these'; -aiḥ + v- → -air v-)
to delude, confuse utterly (vimohayati: causative present 3rd sg.; -i + e- → -y e-)
this (eṣaḥ: nom. sg. masc., referring to kāma; like sa, eṣa/etad irregularly drops its visarga before the following consonant j-, rather than becoming -o)

sentences.l: The-senses, the-mind, the-understanding — its seat, is-called; by-these, deludes, this [enemy], knowledge having-covered, the-embodied-one.
sentences.i: The senses, the mind, and the intellect are said to be desire's seat; through these it deludes the embodied self, veiling its knowledge.
sentences.n: The chain of faculties — indriyāṇi, manaḥ, buddhiḥ, 'the senses, the mind, the understanding' — is named here as kāma's adhiṣṭhānam, 'seat, base of operations', in ascending order (the same hierarchy verse 42 restates as a ranking of what is 'higher'); this diagnostic verse prepares the practical instruction of verse 41.

sentences.t:
तस्मात्त्वमिन्द्रियाण्यादौ नियम्य भरतर्षभ ।
पाप्मानं प्रजहि ह्येनं ज्ञानविज्ञाननाशनम् ॥
sentences.tr:
tasmāt tvam indriyāṇi ādau niyamya bharata-ṛṣabha |
pāpmānam prajahi hi enam jñāna-vijñāna-nāśanam ||

morph.gloss: beginning (ādau: loc. sg. 'at the outset, first')
bull (bharata-ṛṣabha: 'bull among the Bharatas', vocative; -a + ṛ- → -ar-)
to strike down, slay (prajahi: imperative 2nd sg. 'strike down!')
destroyer (jñāna-vijñāna-nāśana: 'destroyer of knowledge and discernment', acc. sg.)

sentences.l: Therefore, you, the-senses, at-the-outset, having-restrained, O bull-among-the-Bharatas — the-evil-thing strike-down, indeed, this, the-destroyer-of-knowledge-and-discernment.
sentences.i: Therefore, bull among the Bharatas, first restrain your senses, and strike down this evil thing that destroys both knowledge and discernment.
sentences.n: The command answering verse 36's question directly: niyamya, 'having restrained' (the senses, the first and outermost of the three faculties named in verse 40), is the starting point, but the real target is pāpmānam ... jñāna-vijñāna-nāśanam, 'the sinful destroyer of knowledge and discernment', i.e. kāma itself — jñāna and vijñāna together (ordinary knowledge and its more discriminating, applied form) name everything desire is said to ruin.

sentences.t:
इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः ।
मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥
sentences.tr:
indriyāṇi parāṇi āhuḥ indriyebhyaḥ param manaḥ |
manasaḥ tu parā buddhiḥ yaḥ buddheḥ parataḥ tu saḥ ||

morph.gloss: higher, superior (parāṇi: acc. pl.; -i + ā- → -y ā-)
to say (āhuḥ: perfect 3rd pl. used as present, 'they say'; -uḥ + i- → -ur i-)
mind (manasaḥ: abl. sg. 'than the mind'; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
higher (nom. sg. fem., agreeing with buddhiḥ)
that, he (nom. sg. masc., i.e. the self)

sentences.l: The-senses, higher, they-say, than-the-senses higher, the-mind; than-the-mind, but, higher, understanding; who than-understanding higher, but, he [is].
sentences.i: The senses, they say, are higher than their objects; the mind is higher than the senses; understanding is higher than the mind; and higher still than understanding is he, the self.
sentences.n: The hierarchy of verse 40 (senses, mind, understanding) is extended one rung further, with each successive term said to be para, 'higher, beyond' the one before: indriya < manas < buddhi < the self (referred to only as saḥ, 'he', not named ātman here, though that is what tradition understands). This ladder is the basis for verse 43's final instruction: since the self stands above understanding, it alone has the standing to master what lies below it.

sentences.t:
एवं बुद्धेः परं बुद्ध्वा संस्तभ्यात्मानमात्मना ।
जहि शत्रुं महाबाहो कामरूपं दुरासदम् ॥
sentences.tr:
evam buddheḥ param buddhvā saṃstabhya ātmānam ātmanā |
jahi śatrum mahā-bāho kāma-rūpam durāsadam ||

morph.gloss: higher, beyond (acc. sg. neut., referring to the self)
to steady, make firm (saṃstabhya: gerund 'having steadied'; saṃstabhya + ā- → saṃstabhyā-)
form (kāma-rūpa: 'having the form of desire', acc. sg., agreeing with śatrum)
hard to approach, hard to overcome (acc. sg.)

sentences.l: Thus, than-understanding, that-which-is-higher having-known, having-steadied the-self by-the-self — slay! the-enemy, O mighty-armed-one, having-the-form-of-desire, hard-to-overcome.
sentences.i: So, knowing that which stands higher than understanding, and steadying the self by the self, slay this enemy in the form of desire, mighty-armed one — hard as it is to overcome.
sentences.n: The chapter closes on the practical command anticipated by verse 42's hierarchy: buddheḥ param, 'that which is higher than understanding' (i.e. the self, ātman), once known (buddhvā), gives one the standing to accomplish ātmānam ātmanā saṃstabhya, 'steadying the self by the self' — a phrase whose apparent circularity states precisely that the higher self must master the lower, psychological one. Durāsadam, 'hard to approach, hard to overcome', is the chapter's last word of respect for the enemy it has spent its final movement (verses 34-43) exposing and commanding Arjuna to destroy.

about: Karmayoga, "the yoga of action," takes up the question Arjuna presses at the outset: if wisdom is better than action, as chapter 2 seemed to say, why does Kṛṣṇa still urge him to fight? Kṛṣṇa answers by denying the premise — no one can remain without acting even for a moment, since everyone is driven to act by the guṇas of nature (verses 4-8) — and then reframes what action itself can be. The middle of the chapter reads the old Vedic cycle of sacrifice as a figure for unattached action: gods and men sustain one another through yajña, and the chain of dependence traced from rain to food to beings is grounded, at last, in brahman itself (verses 9-16). Kṛṣṇa then holds up the free man, exemplified by the philosopher-king Janaka and by Kṛṣṇa's own case, who acts with nothing left to gain, solely for loka-saṃgraha, "the world's welfare" — and asks Arjuna to act the same way, without unsettling those who still cling to the fruits of their own work (verses 17-29). Kṛṣṇa then turns to command Arjuna directly: surrender every action to him and fight, free of anguish (verse 30); those who follow this teaching in faith are freed from action, while those who only carp at it are lost and without understanding (verses 31-32); forcible restraint of the senses accomplishes nothing against a nature that will act as it must (verse 33), so it is passion and aversion themselves, not the senses' contact with their objects, that must be mastered as the true waylayers of the self (verse 34) — which is why one's own dharma, however imperfectly kept, is better than another's well performed (verse 35). The chapter's second half turns to the real obstacle to such freedom: not action itself but kāma, desire, which wears the mask of anger and covers wisdom the way smoke covers fire, dust a mirror, or a caul an unborn child (verses 36-39). Its remedy is a discipline of hierarchy — senses, mind, understanding, and beyond all of these the self — mastered by force of that highest self, with which the chapter closes.
